RoboBench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brain. arXiv:2510.17801.
creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang (Peking University, Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, Fudan University, University of Science and Technology Beijing, Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics)
description: RoboBench is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It defines five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs. The benchmark draws from large-scale real robotic data and in-house collection, and introduces an MLLM-as-world-simulator evaluation framework for assessing long-horizon planning feasibility.
name: RoboBench
publisher: Peking University / Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence
rai:annotationsPerItem: Multiple annotations per item via majority-vote strategy; 20 professionally trained annotators conducted quality inspections. Specific number of annotations per item not stated beyond the quality control process.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom in-house annotation pipeline; no specific third-party annotation platform (e.g., Mechanical Turk) is mentioned. Annotations were performed by 20 professionally trained annotators recruited by the research team.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A two-stage quality control process was adopted: (1) data filtering during construction applying both general and task-specific filters (general criteria address image quality and task validity; sub-benchmarks have tailored rules such as excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks); (2) post-construction validation where 20 professionally trained annotators conducted comprehensive quality inspections validating linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy was also applied: items that all models solve correctly are removed, whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction. For planning tasks, Gemini generated structured annotations (task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata) which were refined by human annotators.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that existing planning data primarily focuses on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing between left-right arm assignments or positional movements, which contributes to model failures in cross-embodiment planning. The benchmark was designed to address biases in prior benchmarks by including diverse embodiments (single-arm, dual-arm, mobile manipulation, humanoid), attribute-rich objects, multi-view scenes, and memory-driven navigation to narrow the sim-to-real gap.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from open-source and in-house robotic datasets. For instruction comprehension, explicit instructions were drawn from daily-life scenarios and implicit instructions were generated by rewriting them using LLMs. For perception reasoning, data was collected across robotic-centric (real robot data with type and view metadata), object-centric (curated static attributes with GPT-generated functional properties), scene-centric (Gemini-segmented video steps with manual annotations), and task-centric (human-labeled bounding boxes) aspects. For generalized planning, a planning pool was built from high-quality robotic videos from multiple large-scale datasets. For affordance prediction, representative frames were sampled from the planning pool and annotated with three types of affordance. For failure analysis, execution-level failures were collected from RoboMIND and labeled by experts, while planning-level failures were synthesized by perturbing correct instructions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include large-scale real-world robotic datasets: RH20T (Fang et al., 2023), Open X-Embodiment (Collaboration et al., 2023), RDT-1B (Liu et al., 2024b), embodied datasets (Liu et al., 2024c), RoboMIND (Wu et al., 2024), AgiBot World (Bu et al., 2025), and navigation data (Yang et al., 2024). In-house collected robotic manipulation videos were also used. Data spans single-arm, dual-arm, and mobile manipulation embodiments across diverse real-world scenes.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Others
rai:dataLimitations: The paper identifies several limitations through experimental findings: (1) planning-level failure data is synthesized rather than collected from real-world failures due to lack of real-world planning failure data; (2) the benchmark reveals that current MLLMs exhibit only superficial embodied reasoning and world-modeling capabilities; (3) execution-level failure diagnosis is extremely challenging even for human evaluators (47.30 vs 80.67 for planning errors), suggesting intrinsic difficulty in this dimension; (4) multi-view inputs yield only modest gains and do not close the gap to human performance.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Planning-level failures were synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order) due to lack of real-world planning failure data. Implicit instructions were generated by rewriting explicit instructions into demand-based requests using LLMs. Items that all models solve correctly were removed from the benchmark; items all models fail were manually reviewed and corrected.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data preprocessing included: (1) extracting frame sequences from robotic videos as standardized inputs; (2) mapping natural language step descriptions to predefined function templates (manipulation and navigation skill lists); (3) instantiating function arguments with objects extracted from step descriptions; (4) converting explicit task instructions into implicit forms using LLMs; (5) standardizing all perception data into multiple-choice QA format; (6) applying general and task-specific filters (image quality, task validity, excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks).
rai:dataSocialImpact: RoboBench provides a comprehensive scaffold to quantify high-level cognition, clarify the role of the embodied brain, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence. The benchmark aims to advance embodied AI systems that can perceive, reason, and act in dynamic, unstructured environments, which has broad implications for robotics applications in real-world settings.
rai:dataUseCases: RoboBench is intended for: (1) systematic evaluation of MLLMs as embodied brains for robotic manipulation; (2) benchmarking high-level cognitive capabilities including instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis; (3) establishing a leaderboard for state-of-the-art MLLMs; (4) providing actionable insights for advancing the embodied brain in robotic AI; (5) guiding the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini (used for video segmentation, generating structured annotations including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata for planning tasks; also used for scene-centric temporal grounding); GPT (used for generating functional properties and distractors for object-centric perception tasks, and for rewriting explicit instructions into implicit forms via LLMs); detection models (used in the annotation pipeline for perception tasks).
